How the orchestrator reads his items (use these; if the code shows a better reading, say so in your notes):
1. Hold-LMB auto swing with the ONE-HANDED axes (hatchet «Топорик», axe «Топор»): after the player walks away the strikes keep landing on the old spot or somewhere else. The two-handed axe («Двуруч.») is right: find what differs (e.g. the feel-1 point-aim depth lock that keeps the strike target while the MOUSE barely moved must also release when the BODY moves; one-handed reach / arc / hand slot). Test: a bot holds LMB, strikes, walks / strafes 0.5-3 m and turns while holding; invariant: every strike lands where the current swing arc from the current body pose first meets material (never the stale point), for all one- and two-handed tools.
2. Branches stay when the stump is finished: branches (or branch items / bodies) that belonged to the part of the tree he chopped away stay floating or are left behind. They must fall with their part or drop to the ground as items. Test: chop a stump / low trunk with branches to the end; invariant: no branch of that tree without support after it, items count conserved.
3. Cutting the stump top: the piece that falls off is a perfect cylinder; it must carry the real cut geometry with every notch (its bottom = the stump's top cut surface, its sides = the trunk as it was). Test: piece mesh volume = the volume removed above the cut (+-2 %), and the distance between the piece's cut face and the stump's cut face <= one canvas cell.
4. Trajectory: replace the line look by ENTRY / EXIT holes: where the tool's strike shape goes into the material, where it would come out if the tool were infinitely strong («как по маслу»), and the hole between: red, semi-transparent, drawn on the front (entry) face and the back (exit) face, the inside part darker (it is behind material), visible through objects. Cheap (<= ~1 ms per frame in WebGL2, few draw calls); every tool. It must not jump while walking: test = walk straight / strafe at constant speed aiming at a trunk; the predicted entry point moves smoothly (frame-to-frame jump beyond the body's own motion <= 1 cm; save the series).
5. Stone texture swims / shimmers when a stone moves (carried, falling, fragments): the texture must stick to the stone (object space, not world space). Test: the texture coordinate at a fixed local vertex is the same before / after moving + rotating the body; browser shot pair.
6. Glass and ice shatter completely too easily. Study the physics FROM SOURCES (WebSearch / WebFetch; cite them in notes): brittle fracture (Griffith / Irwin, fracture energy G_c = K_IC^2 / E, K_IC of soda-lime glass, ice, quartz), the size effect, blunt impact on thick glass (Hertzian cone cracks), thin panes breaking in bending. Then make glass and ice (and quartz) behave like the stone class: a big block barely reacts to one blow (a local chip / cone, a crack); cracks spread over repeated blows; pieces break off where cracks join; a full split needs energy ~ G_c x the cross-section, so it scales with size; thin sheets and panes do shatter. Reuse the stone fracture path, not a separate shatter hack. Tests: 1 m ice block, 0.5 m glass block, 5 mm glass pane, quartz crystal vs hatchet / sledgehammer / god blows: number of blows to the first piece and to a full split, crack length per blow, with the source numbers in the notes.
7. Frame spikes / freezes when hitting brick and others, and even when just walking (web build). Find them in the browser (shader compile on first use, physics body or mesh creation, canvas / CSG rebuild, streaming, GC); fix (warm-up at load, spread work over frames, cache). Measure with a scripted walk + hits on brick / stone / wood / glass: per-frame script CPU and the count of frames with one job > 8 ms, before / after; plus wall frame time in the browser (SwiftShader is slow, compare like with like).
8. Stone pieces that break off stay fixed or move toward the blow. A share of the blow energy goes into kinetic energy: pieces fly off a little, away from the hit (along the blow and the outward face normal); small pieces further, big slabs tip. Deterministic. Test: N breaks on several stones: every piece's initial velocity points away from the tool (dot > 0) and 1/2 m v^2 matches the chosen energy share (+-10 %).
9. The delay between the hit and the break: measure contact frame -> visible change (frames, ms) in solo and 2-process; cut it to the contact frame where possible: pre-compute the carve / fracture for the predicted contact during the wind-up (LMB held) and apply on contact; the server stays the authority (a different server result corrects the visual). Test: frames from contact to the visible change, before / after, solo and 2-process.
10. Shovel load: switching from the shovel to the bare hand moves the soil into the hand. The load belongs to the TOOL: it stays on the shovel when switching hands / slots and in the inventory, and the shovel shows it there. The load is a composition: litres per material (soil, gravel, turf / grass, sand, clay...) shown separately in the HUD and the item panel; dumping puts back each material (mass conserved per material). Tests: dig 8 L, switch to the hand -> hand empty, back -> 8 L; into the inventory and back -> 8 L; a mixed dig -> per-material litres sum to the total, conserved on dump.
11. Water sounds missing in places: find water (river, lake, pools, range troughs, liquids) without ambient / footstep / splash sound; fix with one cheap system (distance-culled emitters along water, steps in shallow water, splash when things fall in). Test: a bot visits every water kind and checks a sound would play there (headless: the emitter / player is active within its range).
12. Every 3D tool and item mesh (hands, tools of every shape x material, items, pieces) has no holes: a headless test checks watertightness (each edge shared by exactly two triangles with opposite winding, no degenerate triangles, normals outward) and shots of each tool from a few angles; fix the holes it finds.
13. Ground texture: square grass / dirt edges after digging (img2) and blocky grass patches on heaps (img3). Find the cause; fix it only if the fix is small and safe (e.g. mask filtering / edge noise); a full layered ground is a later design wave, so otherwise write the cause and numbers in your notes. Test: max colour / alpha jump across dig-cell borders on dug, regrown and heap ground (extend the feel-1 item 18 check).
